findings.message: The saga-iter-3 rewrite of this scenario to a hard-kill-then-restart crash-recovery probe RESOLVES the prior non-observability finding (TL-BDD-01): the hard-kill is a controllable test action and post-restart resolution is a deterministic observable, so 'durably committed at ack' now has a real measurement point. One residual C2 gap remains. The Then 'after the Mapping Store restarts the issued short code SHALL still resolve to the original URL' is an in-scenario async wait on store-restart completion with no declared numeric timeout or polling ceiling. A step-definition author cannot bound how long to wait for the store to come back and the code to resolve before the test fails, leaving the assertion environment-sensitive. This differs from BDD.01.03.44fe, where restoration is a Given precondition already true and the live redirect carries @threshold:PRD.01.perf.redirectp95 — here the restart-and-resolve is a live When/Then transition with no bound.
findings.recommendation: Attach a named threshold key to the restart-and-resolve wait so the polling ceiling is declared even with a PRD-deferred value: bound the post-restart resolution under the RTO key implied by EARS.01.04.5e5b (RTO <= 30 min), or carry @threshold:PRD.01.perf.redirectp95 on the resolve assertion once the store is back. A named threshold key satisfies C2 as a declared numeric bound.
